record.paper_title: Open Problems on Connectivity of Fibers with Positive Margins in Multi-dimensional Contingency Tables
record.original_question: Let t = A_T(n_obs) be the margin vector for a contingency-table model, suppose t_ℓ > 0 for some row index ℓ, and let F_T = {n in N^k : A_T(n) = A_T(n_obs)}. Develop an algorithm that computes, in terms of set inclusion, a minimum set of moves M connecting all tables in F_T and that is faster than computing a full Markov basis via geometry-based algorithms such as those implemented in 4ti2.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. With tℓ > 0 for some row index ℓ, develop an algorithm to compute a minimum set of moves M in terms of inclusion which connects all tables in FT faster than computing a full Markov basis via algorithms using geometry such as implemented in 4ti2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a log-linear contingency-table model defined by a configuration matrix $A_T \in \mathbb{Z}^{d\times k}$ acting on count vectors by $n \mapsto A_T(n)$. For an observed count vector $n_{\mathrm{obs}} \in \mathbb{N}^k$, let $t = A_T(n_{\mathrm{obs}}) \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ be its margin vector, and define the fiber
$$F_T \;=\; \{\, n \in \mathbb{N}^k : A_T(n) = A_T(n_{\mathrm{obs}})\,\}.$$
A move is an integer vector $m \in \ker_{\mathbb{Z}} A_T$, and a set of moves $M$ is said to connect $F_T$ if for every pair $n, n' \in F_T$ there exists a sequence $n = n_0, n_1, \dots, n_r = n'$ with each $n_i \in F_T$ and $n_i - n_{i-1} \in \pm M$. A Markov basis is such a connecting set $M$ that works for every fiber, and it can be computed (e.g.\ by Gröbner / geometry-based methods such as those implemented in 4ti2) but at substantial cost.

Assume that the margin $t$ has at least one strictly positive coordinate, i.e.\ $t_\ell > 0$ for some index $\ell$.

Problem. Design an algorithm that, taking the configuration $A_T$ and the margin $t$ (with $t_\ell > 0$) as input, outputs a set of moves $M \subseteq \ker_{\mathbb{Z}} A_T$ which
(i) connects the single fiber $F_T$, and
(ii) is minimal with respect to set inclusion among all such connecting sets,
and which runs strictly faster (in worst-case or practical complexity) than computing a full Markov basis of $A_T$ via geometry-based Markov-basis algorithms such as those implemented in 4ti2.
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search returns related work on Markov bases for contingency tables with positive margins (e.g., quotient-ideal approaches, minimal invariant Markov bases, and bounded-table subbases), but no source clearly presents a general algorithm that produces an inclusion-minimal connecting set for fibers with at least one positive margin coordinate strictly faster than a full geometry-based Markov-basis computation (such as 4ti2). The status of this specific algorithmic problem appears to remain unresolved in the sources retrieved.

status_evidence.title: Markov Chains, Quotient Ideals, and Connectivity with Positive Margins
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses fibers connected by subsets of a Markov basis under positive-margin conditions, leveraging quotient ideals.
status_evidence.claim: Related theoretical framework; does not provide a general faster-than-4ti2 algorithm for inclusion-minimal connecting sets.

status_evidence.title: Markov bases and subbases for bounded contingency tables
status_evidence.snippet: Studies subbases of Markov bases that suffice to connect restricted fibers (e.g., bounded tables).
status_evidence.claim: Addresses related connectivity-with-subbases questions but not the requested faster general algorithm.

status_evidence.title: Minimal Basis for a Connected Markov Chain over 3x3xK Contingency Tables with Fixed Two-Dimensional Marginals
status_evidence.snippet: Computes minimal connecting sets in the special 3x3xK case.
status_evidence.claim: Solves a special case but not the general problem.
